h1: The 6 Best Smart Speakers With Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six smart displays from Amazon and Google, sorted by screen size, sound, camera options and smart home reach.
summary: The Amazon Echo Show 8 is the best smart speaker with a screen for most homes: an 8.7 inch HD display with spatial audio at a mid-range price. The Echo Show 11 suits large rooms, the Show 5 fits bedside tables, and the Nest Hub is the camera-free Google choice. The Echo Hub is a control panel, not a media speaker.
intro: Shoppers choose a smart display by screen size, then find out the real decision was the ecosystem. An Echo Show behaves nothing like a Nest Hub, and the smart plugs, lights and music subscriptions you already own quietly decide which one feels useful by day two. Hardware specs matter far less than whether your accounts and devices fit the assistant behind the glass.

Six displays are covered here, judged on spec sheets and the feedback of people who use them daily. We ranked them on screen size, audio, camera and privacy options, smart home protocol support and how well each fits the room it is meant for. The Echo Spot and a renewed Nest Hub Max were left out as narrower or less certain buys.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 8 (newest model), Vibrant HD 8.7" Display with Spatial Audio, Designed for Alexa+, Graphite
products.verdict: The right size, the right sound and a sensible price for almost any room.
products.description:
The Echo Show 8 has an 8.7 inch HD display, spatial audio and design for Alexa+, at a mid-range price. Eight inches is the size where recipes, video calls and photos become readable from a counter, and spatial audio makes the speaker useful for music rather than just timers.

It ranks first because it fits almost any room without taking over. The Show 11 is bigger and costs more, and the Show 5 gives up the screen for a nightstand fit.

Buy it for one versatile smart display. The caveats are that it runs only on Alexa and is smaller than the Show 11. Skip it if your household runs on Google services, since your routines will not carry over.
products.idealFor: Most homes wanting one versatile smart display.
products.skipIf: Your household runs on Google services.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 11 (newest model), Vibrant Full-HD 11" Display with Spatial Audio, Designed for Alexa+, Graphite
products.verdict: The newest Echo display, with an 11 inch Full HD screen for bigger rooms.
products.description:
The Echo Show 11 has an 11 inch Full HD display, spatial audio and the newest 2025 design for Alexa+. A larger, sharper screen reads from across a room, which helps in open plans and for photo slideshows.

It ranks second because it sits in a higher price bracket and needs more counter space. The Show 8 gives most of the experience for less.

Buy it for open plan rooms and photo or video fans who sit well back from the screen. Skip it if you have a small counter or bedside table. Placement matters more with a bigger screen, so measure before ordering, and plan for the extra cable and stand footprint. The bigger speaker cabinet also gives fuller sound than the Show 8 for music, which is the other reason to step up.
products.idealFor: Open plan rooms and photo or video fans.
products.skipIf: You have a small counter or bedside table.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 5 (newest model), Smart Display, Designed for Alexa+, Charcoal
products.verdict: The small display that fits a nightstand without crowding it.
products.description:
The Echo Show 5 is a 5.5 inch display with twice the bass of the prior generation and Alexa+ built in, in the lower price tier. A small footprint suits a bedside table or desk, and the extra bass helps a compact speaker.

It ranks third because the screen is too small for recipes or video and the speaker is modest. It beats the larger displays on price and bedside fit.

Buy it for bedside tables and small desks. Skip it if you want to follow recipes or watch video. Think of it as an alarm clock with assistant features, good for timers, weather and music at night. Because Alexa+ is built in, it handles the same routines as bigger Echo models, without the footprint.
pros: Twice the bass of prior model
products.skipIf: You want to follow recipes or watch video.

products.name: Google Nest Hub 7" Smart Display with Google Assistant (2nd Gen), Chalk
products.verdict: A camera free Google display with sleep sensing for bedrooms.
products.description:
The Google Nest Hub second generation has a 7 inch display, no camera, Google Assistant and Sleep Sensing. A camera-free design is a privacy plus in a bedroom, and Sleep Sensing adds a bedtime feature.

It ranks fourth because it cannot do video calls and works only in Google's ecosystem. It suits Google homes best.

Buy it for a Google household that values privacy and wants a simple display. Skip it if you need video calls or Alexa. In a bedroom, the absence of a camera is a feature, not a flaw. The 7 inch screen shows photos and weather, but it will not match the Echo Show 8 for video, and it will not carry Alexa routines from another household.
products.idealFor: Google households that value camera free privacy.
products.skipIf: You need video calls or Alexa.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 15 (newest model), Full HD 15.6" Kitchen Hub with Built-In Fire TV, Designed for Alexa+
products.verdict: A wall mount sized kitchen hub with Fire TV built in.
products.description:
The Echo Show 15 has a 15.6 inch Full HD display with Fire TV built in and a kitchen hub design. A big wall screen works as a family organizer with calendars, notes and video, and Fire TV means it can show a program.

It ranks fifth because it needs wall space and sits in a higher price bracket. It is the largest screen here.

Buy it for a busy family kitchen with a free wall. Skip it if counter space is tight. Mounting it needs planning, and the listing is built around a wall hang. Fire TV adds streaming apps, but it is not a replacement for a main television, and the price sits well above the smaller Echo Show models.
products.idealFor: Busy family kitchens with a free wall.

products.name: Amazon Echo Hub (newest model), 8", Zigbee, Matter, Thread, Compatible with Thousands of Devices
products.verdict: A smart home control panel, not a media speaker.
products.description:
The Echo Hub is an 8 inch control panel supporting Zigbee, Matter and Thread, with no camera and compatibility with thousands of devices. It acts as a dashboard for a smart home rather than a media device.

It ranks last because it is not a media speaker and cannot do video calling. It suits smart home owners who want a control panel.

Buy it if you manage many connected devices from a wall panel. Skip it if you want music or video calls. Its protocol support reduces the need for separate bridges, and the wall panel layout suits a hallway. It has no camera, so it keeps video calling off the table, and it will not replace a speaker for music.
products.idealFor: Smart home owners wanting a control dashboard.
products.skipIf: You want music or video calls.

whatMatters.detail: A smart display is the front end for either Alexa or Google Assistant, so your existing accounts and devices matter more than the hardware. Switching later means re-adding every light and speaker. Check which assistant your current smart plugs and music service work best with before you buy, and stay within one ecosystem if you can.

Sizes here range from 5.5 inches to 15.6 inches. Small screens work for alarms and glances, while video and recipes need 8 inches or more. Think about viewing distance, and match the display to the room using the size in the listing title. The Show 8 and Show 11 cover most counters and open rooms.

Some displays carry a camera for video calls, while the Nest Hub and Echo Hub do not. A camera adds convenience but also a privacy question for bedrooms. Read the listing for a camera line, and prefer a camera-free model for sleeping spaces. If you want video calls, a camera model like the Show 8 is necessary.

Matter, Thread and Zigbee are the standards many modern devices use to talk to a hub. A display that supports them can control more gear without extra bridges. The Echo Hub lists all three in its title, so check for them if you own many connected devices, and verify any other model before you rely on it.

A smart display is still a speaker, and small ones sound thin. Spatial audio and extra bass on a larger cabinet help music fill a room. Look for audio features named in the listing rather than vague words like rich sound. The Show 8 and 11 list spatial audio, and the Show 5 lists extra bass.

faq.q: Can I mix Alexa and Google displays in one home?
faq.a: You can, but they will not share routines or device control. Pick one assistant for the devices you use most and add a second only for a specific room, such as a kitchen.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a smart display?
faq.a: Choosing by screen size before checking the ecosystem. If your smart plugs and music service favor the other assistant, the display will feel limited, whatever the screen size or price.

faq.q: Is the Echo Show 11 worth it over the Show 8?
faq.a: Only if you view the screen from across the room or care about Full HD photos. For counters and desks, the Show 8 gives most of the experience for less.

faq.q: Do I need a hub if I buy the Echo Hub?
faq.a: The Echo Hub lists Zigbee, Matter and Thread support, so it can act as the hub for many compatible devices without a separate bridge. Check compatibility with your specific devices before you buy, since not every sensor speaks Thread.

faq.q: Where should I place a smart display?
faq.a: Keep it near a power outlet and within Wi-Fi range, away from steam and direct sunlight. A shelf at eye level works best, and a kitchen hub like the Show 15 needs a safe wall spot.

faq.q: Can a display with no camera still make calls?
faq.a: Audio calls may work through the assistant, but video calling needs a camera. Camera-free models like the Nest Hub are not suited to video chat, so choose an Echo Show if you want it, rather than the Echo Hub.

finalTake: The Echo Show 8 is the right smart display for most homes, since it balances size, sound and price. Choose the Show 11 for open rooms, the Nest Hub for a camera-free Google bedroom and the Echo Hub for a control panel. Pick the ecosystem before the screen.
